:::{#def-empty-set}
#### Empty set

The **empty set**
[@wikipedia_empty_set], denoted $\emptyset$,
is the set that has no elements.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-empty-set-notation}
#### Other notation for the empty set

Other sources write $\set{}$ for $\emptyset$
[@wikipedia_empty_set].
Some sources call it the **null set**,
but in measure theory a "null set" usually means a set of [measure zero](measures.qmd#def-measure-zero),
which need not be empty.
For example, the interval $[0, 0] = \set{0}$ has length $0 - 0 = 0$,
so it is a null set in that sense,
but it is not empty, because $0 \in \set{0}$.

:::
